clue.text: Some learn to cope with a bird

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of cope and finishes inside with

explanation.surface: A beginner birdkeeper finds that some people simply learn to put up with a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sits in plain sight across 'coPE WITh'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewit is another name for the lapwing, a crested plover of farmland named for its call.

clue.text: Tongue no longer available— it's put away

blocks.note: the language spoken in Poland
as a dish is off the menu when it has run out

explanation.surface: A restaurant has run out of ox tongue, now cleared from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' reads as the meat on the menu, but it is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is informal for eating it all up quickly, which is exactly what polishing off a plate means.

clue.text: To rouse means talking to a man

indicators.note: talking means the words are to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

blocks.note: a way is a means of doing something
Ken is a man's name, the one being addressed

explanation.surface: Someone shaking a sleeper awake by talking to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Said to a man named Ken, 'Way, Ken!' sounds just like the answer, which is pronounced WAY-ken.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for bringing someone out of sleep; the infinitive 'to rouse' matches the base verb form.

clue.text: Work hard getting pictures up on the screen, we hear

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
what we hear is a sound, so a word spelt differently but pronounced the same is wanted

blocks.note: pictures are works of art
a veil screens a face

explanation.surface: A projectionist or film-maker toils to get images onto a cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places one piece after the other. The surface's 'pictures up on the screen' suggests the cinema, but pictures are art turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is a literary verb meaning to labour or toil painfully, so it swaps for working hard.

clue.text: Nickname thus applied to fuel

blocks.note: so means in this way, thus
a briquet, or briquette, is a block of compressed coal dust burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: A name is given, in this way, to some kind of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a familiar or humorous name given to a person, which is what a nickname is.

clue.text: Coach-building

blocks.note: first meaning: to train or teach someone
second meaning: the building where pupils are taught

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes it look like the trade of making coaches for horses or buses; split it and there are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to train or educate; as a noun it is the premises where lessons take place.

clue.text: Kills with a look

blocks.note: first meaning: slaughters brutally
second meaning: from rhyming slang

explanation.surface: A killer whose glance alone is deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it: 'have a butcher's' means 'have a look' because hook rhymes with look.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterer savagely kills, and in London slang a quick glance is a butcher's, from the rhyme on hook.

clue.text: One grid could be cut

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else once rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword grid that might be trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb acting on the grid, but it is the definition, in its social sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, deliberately refusing to acknowledge them in public.

clue.text: Upper class aristocrat comes in uninvited to investigate the interior

indicators.note: something that comes in enters another thing and ends up inside it

blocks.note: U is the standard label for upper-class usage
to pry is to look into matters that are none of your business
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A posh nobleman barges in, unasked, to snoop around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun sense; the phrase can also be an adverb, but here it names the inland region.
explanation.definitionFit: Up country is the inland region away from the coast, so it names the interior of a land.

clue.text: Article — note the subject

blocks.note: the definite article
me, or mi, is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An editor reminds a writer what a newspaper article is meant to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic a piece of writing or talk deals with, which is its subject.

clue.text: At once solid, spherical and injurious

blocks.note: first meaning: immediately, without hesitation
second meaning, read literally: resembling a cannonball, which is solid, round and harmful

explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes a cannonball or lead shot, so something with those qualities is literally like one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly or immediately, from the speed of a fired bullet or cannonball.

clue.text: Henry's installed in pleasant, suitable position

indicators.note: something installed in a place is fitted inside it

blocks.note: nice means pleasant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry has been settled into an agreeable job that suits him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a person's name, but it is the physics unit abbreviated to H.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place exactly fitted to someone's talents, a comfortable and appropriate spot.

clue.text: Alter one's attitude and give an encore

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for changing one's opinion or manner
second meaning, literal: perform a further song for the audience

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to change one's views or behaviour, usually becoming humbler; literally, a performer giving an extra song does it too.

clue.text: I left the Spanish capital, returning to Delphi

definitions.note: Delphi stands for its famous oracle

indicators.note: the letter I has left, so it is taken out of the next word
returning means going back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: el is the Spanish for the
the Egyptian capital city

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves a Spanish city and heads back to Greece, to Delphi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish capital' suggests Madrid, but the phrase splits: 'the Spanish' is the article and 'capital' is another city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the seat of the most celebrated ancient Greek oracle, the priestess of Apollo consulted for prophecy.

clue.text: Cattle are shaping to lock horns

indicators.note: shaping means forming into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bulls in a field are squaring up for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to argue or dispute heatedly, the figurative sense of two animals clashing horns.

clue.text: An old-fashioned king at first changed imperceptibly

indicators.note: at first places this piece at the front, ahead of the others

blocks.note: GR, for Georgius Rex, is King George's cipher
the indefinite article
dated means out of fashion

explanation.surface: An outmoded monarch who quietly altered over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gradated passes from one shade or stage to the next by tiny steps, so the shift is barely noticed.

clue.text: Improved appearance of sweet (including most of another) with inversion

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
including means taking something in, so one word holds another
an inversion turns things upside down, so in a down entry the whole is read upward

blocks.note: pud, short for pudding, is a sweet course
dessert is another word for the sweet course

explanation.surface: An instruction for making a sweet look better, set out like a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sweet goes outside, split after its second letter, and the second, minus its T, sits inside before everything is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress something up is to make it look smarter or more attractive by adorning it.

clue.text: Dedicate everything “With love to Tom — East”

blocks.note: all means everything
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a tom is a male cat
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: An author writes a dedication: everything, with love, to Tom in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a book's dedication page; Tom is not a person but an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dedicate funds or time to a purpose is to set them aside for it, which is to allot or assign them.

clue.text: Correspond comprehensively, off and on

blocks.note: to fit is to match or correspond
fully means completely

explanation.surface: Someone writes letters thoroughly, but only now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspond' suggests writing letters, but here it means to match.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitfully means in irregular bursts with interruptions, intermittently, as in sleeping fitfully.

clue.text: Alone abroad and without a PA

blocks.note: first meaning: by oneself, with nobody's help
second meaning, read literally: with no aide, a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A busy executive travels overseas alone, with no assistant to help.
explanation.walkthrough: A PA (personal assistant) is an aide, so being without one is being literally un-aided; 'abroad' just sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without help from anyone is doing it alone, single-handed and independently.

clue.text: Retreating Englishman is inside the breakwater

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters run from right to left
one piece is inside, so it sits within the other

blocks.note: split as English, abbreviated ENG, and man, here the name Roy

explanation.surface: An Englishman backs away and shelters behind a sea wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Englishman' looks like one word but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out from a beach into the sea to check erosion, a type of breakwater.

clue.text: Wire had to be twisted into a rope

indicators.note: being twisted bends the letters out of their order, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the first four letters to be rearranged
the other three letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Strands of wire must be wound together to make a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' does double duty in the surface but is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawhide is untanned leather, and a rope or whip plaited from it is also called a rawhide.

clue.text: Boy meets girl once in India

definitions.note: a region once wholly in India

blocks.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is a colloquial word for a girl

explanation.surface: A romance of boy meets girl, set long ago in the days of the Raj.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal was a province of British India; at partition in 1947 its east became part of Pakistan, now Bangladesh.

clue.text: Andrew's pigeons determined to head south and seek wider horizons

indicators.note: determined here means settled or worked out, so the letters are fixed into a new order
to head means to go at the front, before everything else

blocks.note: the compass abbreviation
the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pigeon fancier's birds are set on flying south to explore further afield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head south' reads as flying southwards, but it puts the compass letter at the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread one's wings is an idiom for venturing out and trying new things, like a young bird leaving the nest.

clue.text: Central European wife is absorbed in craft

indicators.note: something absorbed in another is taken inside it

blocks.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft
the standard abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman from central Europe is engrossed in her handicrafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a hobby, but it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland lies in the centre of Europe, so a person or thing from there is Central European.

clue.text: Indian politician — he acquired a name for turning up at football

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading the letters from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
RU is Rugby Union, a code of football

explanation.surface: A statesman made his name by appearing at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three letters are turned; the football piece follows them as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru led India's independence movement and became its first prime minister in 1947.

clue.text: Chamois heading off reptile ...

indicators.note: with its heading off, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a lizard is a scaly reptile

explanation.surface: A mountain goat chases a reptile away.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots run on into the next clue, which uses the same trick of heading off in a different sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the Pyrenean variety of chamois, an agile goat-antelope of European mountains.

clue.text: ... in pain, heading us off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a creature suffering as it heads us off.
explanation.walkthrough: After the previous clue, 'heading off' looks like a deletion again; here 'heading us' is the material and 'off' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguished means suffering severe distress or torment, physical or mental.

clue.text: Veronica has joined expedition— we will ...

blocks.note: expedition can mean promptness or speed
contracted to we'll, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A woman named Veronica has signed up for an expedition, and the rest follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name but is a plant genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the botanical genus of the speedwells, small plants with blue flowers.

clue.text: ... fit out expedition's leader, Sally

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a sally is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Completing the previous clue: we will kit out the expedition's leader, a woman called Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a name, but a sally is a witticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip a party is to supply it with the gear it needs, which is to fit it out.
